scope: Interpreting monetary columns of the budget table
description: The budget table holds two distinct monetary measures: amount is the amount budgeted (planned allocation) for a spending category of an event, while spent is the amount actually spent against that line. Questions phrased as 'amount budgeted' use amount; questions phrased as 'spent'/'money spent' use spent. Substituting one for the other yields incorrect results.

scope: Matching a person named in a question to the member table
description: A member's full name is formed from the member's first_name and last_name. A person referred to by full name (for example 'Maya Mclean' or 'Connor Hilton') matches the member whose first_name and last_name are those two tokens. Asking for 'full name' means returning both name parts together; asking for 'last name' means returning last_name only.

scope: Date filtering, range filtering and year extraction on events
description: event_date is stored as an ISO-8601 date-time string of the form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS (19 characters). The calendar year of an event is the leading four characters of the string. Event dates in the data fall within 2019 and 2020.

income.source takes exactly four values: 'Dues', 'Fundraising', 'School Appropration' and 'Sponsorship'. Note that the third value is spelled 'School Appropration' in the data (missing an 'i'); filters must use the stored spelling. Values are case-sensitive.

scope: Filtering or grouping events by status
description: event.status takes exactly three values: 'Open', 'Closed' and 'Planning'. A 'closed' event means status='Closed'; values are case-sensitive.

scope: Filtering or grouping events by the kind of activity
description: event.type takes eight values: Budget, Community Service, Election, Game, Guest Speaker, Meeting, Registration and Social. A 'game' event means type='Game'; values are case-sensitive.

scope: Filtering or grouping budget and spending by category
description: budget.category takes five values: Advertisement, Club T-Shirts, Food, Parking and Speaker Gifts. Spending 'for food' means category='Food'; values are case-sensitive.

scope: Interpreting the word 'category' in questions about events
description: The phrase 'category of events' is ambiguous in this database: it can refer to event.type, the kind of activity an event represents (Meeting, Guest Speaker, Game, ...), or to budget.category, the spending category of the event's budget lines (Food, Parking, Advertisement, ...). Both readings are grounded. The intended meaning depends on whether the question concerns the nature of the activity or the budget/spending dimension.

scope: Interpreting who counts as a 'member' of the club
description: member.position takes the values 'Member', 'President', 'Vice President', 'Treasurer', 'Secretary' and 'Inactive'. 'Members' in the ordinary sense means position='Member' (regular members, 26 people); officers hold separate position values and 'Inactive' marks former members. Include officers only when the question explicitly asks for them.
member.t_shirt_size takes the values 'Small', 'Medium', 'Large' and 'X-Large'. 'Medium' is stored literally as 'Medium'; values are case-sensitive.

scope: Answering whether a member attended an event
description: A row in the attendance table for a (member, event) pair means that member attended that event. The absence of a matching row means there is no recorded attendance. Attendance is matched through member identity (first_name plus last_name) and event identity (event_name).

scope: Joining members to majors, departments and colleges
description: One of the 33 members has no linked major (link_to_major is empty). Any join from member to major drops that member, which matters when listing 'all' members by academic affiliation.
expense.approved is 'true' for 31 of the 32 expense records and empty for one record; the empty value means no approval value was recorded rather than 'not approved'.
